answer: Give every new identity a narrow inlet into the economy instead of the open ocean: a fresh agent may only take small, low-value jobs, and its earning cap rises only after many epochs of completed work verified by unrelated peers. Trust is earned as a non-transferable history, not bought — a velvet rope that lifts slowly. An attacker spinning up ten thousand sock puppets must fund months of real, useful work for each before any of them can touch a valuable transaction, so the cost of a fake army scales with time and effort while honest agents pass through once.
